Meeting records [Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1liPApVM0qvFe6X6gzNBgTvjlLZfBMzQZYCwOnCDz1rA/edit?usp=drive_web&tab=t.2eq7e5gytbs9) 

### Summary

Meeting reviewed skills matrix tool development for finance alignment and future operational capabilities via data integration.

**Tool Functionality Review**  
Demonstration showed dashboard capabilities for resource allocation. Initial prototype development demonstrated significant progress and potential for tracking regional skill levels.

**Finance Data Requirements**  
Alignment of internal terminology with finance categories for automated reporting was prioritized. The group decided to pause health report updates until tool completion.

**Technical Integration Strategy**  
Plans for integrating BigQuery and Salesforce were established to move beyond manual spreadsheets. Security controls and access levels ensure sensitive information remains protected.

*Rate this Summary:* [Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4YkxrBAaiTVqYCi?isGoogler=false&isHelpful=true) or [Not Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4YkxrBAaiTVqYCi?isGoogler=false&isHelpful=false)

### Decisions

We've **updated the Decisions section** using your feedback.

Let us know what you think: [Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5p6FWBVWvynleNU?isGoogler=no&isHelpful=yes) or [Not Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5p6FWBVWvynleNU?isGoogler=no&isHelpful=no)

## ALIGNED

* **Granular resource allocation tracking adopted** The team will adopt a granular approach to tracking resource allocation, separating work into categories such as "Run" and "Change" to meet finance reporting requirements.

* **Self-service data entry model adopted** Employees will input their own skill and allocation data, while managers retain oversight and override authority to ensure data accuracy.

* **Tool rollout strategy defined** The team will release the initial version of the tool to managers to provide immediate value before implementing further enhancements.

* **Health report revamp cancelled** The project to revamp the existing health report is cancelled, with the team choosing to wait until the new skills matrix tool is fully implemented.

### Next steps

- [ ] \[Richard Crossley\] Contact Carl: Discuss Salesforce integration with Carl and his team.

- [ ] \[Richard Crossley\] Consult Oscar: Consult Oscar regarding hosting requirements, architect support, and access to necessary API tokens.

- [ ] \[Damak Varshney\] Draft Tool Plan: Document the development roadmap and feature phases for the application.

- [ ] \[Richard Crossley\] Schedule Meeting: Create a calendar placeholder for a follow-up session in 2 weeks. Adjust the date forward if project progress allows.

- [ ] \[Richard Crossley\] Consult Damak: Meet with Damak to review project status. Prepare tangible material for the next group discussion.

### Details

*Did the screenshots in this section make your notes [better](https://goo.gle/44IH7J9) or [worse](https://goo.gle/4b5ZWtJ)?*

* **Meeting Objective and Overview**: Richard Crossley opened the meeting to review the trajectory of the "skills matrix" tool being developed by Damak Varshney, transitioning it from a prototype into a functional application ([00:01:31](#00:01:31)). Richard Crossley noted that Damak Varshney had already progressed significantly beyond the initial proof of concept, and the current goal was to confirm the direction and capabilities of the tool before further enhancement ([00:00:38](#00:00:38)).

* **Finance Department Data Requirements**: Jane Hill explained that the finance team requires detailed resource allocation data at the individual level to calculate the cost of supporting different products ([00:03:23](#00:03:23)). This includes categorizing work into "Run," "Change," and "Regulatory" classifications to allow finance to understand support expenses and potentially leverage tax offsetting for new developments ([00:04:22](#00:04:22)). Jane Hill shared a template provided by the finance team that highlights the need for aligning individuals to specific products and projects ([00:03:23](#00:03:23)) ([00:06:05](#00:06:05)).

  ![][image1]

* **Tool Demonstration and Capabilities**: Damak Varshney showcased the current application, which features an executive dashboard for viewing regional splits, a regional heat map, and a skill deep-dive feature ([00:07:03](#00:07:03)). The tool currently pulls employee profile data from Google Chat but requires Salesforce connectors to automate allocation data ([00:08:03](#00:08:03)). Jane Hill, Richard Crossley, and Scott Bolnick expressed significant enthusiasm for the tool's capabilities, with Richard Crossley noting that Damak Varshney built the application in approximately two days ([00:09:02](#00:09:02)).

  ![][image2]

* **Data Entry and Oversight Processes**: Regarding data input, Damak Varshney proposed empowering L1 representatives to enter their own product and skill information, subject to manager approval and oversight ([00:09:34](#00:09:34)). Richard Crossley suggested a self-certification process where individuals update their own values, with leads maintaining the authority to override them if they disagree, which would also help highlight regional discrepancies in skill level definitions ([00:11:23](#00:11:23)).

  ![][image3]

* **Expansion into Training and Operational Management**: Scott Bolnick and Richard Crossley discussed expanding the tool to track training plans and certifications, potentially replacing fragmented spreadsheets ([00:13:01](#00:13:01)). Richard Crossley mentioned that future iterations could integrate availability data from Day Force to assist with capacity management and coverage planning, while Scott Bolnick suggested incorporating Salesforce case volume data to better analyze individual productivity ([00:13:56](#00:13:56)).

  ![][image4]

* **Finance Terminology Mapping**: Jane Hill and Richard Crossley discussed the need to map internal terminology—such as Business As Usual (BAU) and project work—to the finance team's preferred terms, like "Run" and "Change," to facilitate automatic reporting. The group agreed that the tool should accommodate these mappings to eliminate the need for manual reconciliation of finance data ([00:17:11](#00:17:11)). Damak Varshney noted that the tool includes an admin center to control products, skills, and team management ([00:18:04](#00:18:04)).

  ![][image5]

* **Access and Security Controls**: Scott Bolnick and Damak Varshney discussed the importance of varying access levels within the application ([00:18:45](#00:18:45)). Damak Varshney confirmed that the tool is already designed to allow restricted views, ensuring that users can only access their specific employee vaults while administrators retain full visibility of the data ([00:19:34](#00:19:34)).

  ![][image6]

* **Technical Implementation and Immediate Next Steps**: Richard Crossley identified immediate next steps, including integrating Astra Single Sign-On and moving the application from Damak Varshney's local machine to a hosted environment ([00:20:21](#00:20:21)). The team confirmed the tool is built using the Google Gemini Command Line Interface (CLI) Enterprise. Richard Crossley emphasized the importance of continuing development to ensure the tool provides immediate value to managers ([00:21:14](#00:21:14)).

  ![][image7]

* **Data Integration and Scaling**: The team discussed the need to transition away from Google Sheets and obtain direct access to BigQuery to pull data from Salesforce and Jira ([00:25:12](#00:25:12)). Jane Hill decided to pause the revamp of the health report until this tool is completed, as it could eventually automate health reporting ([00:26:05](#00:26:05)). Richard Crossley noted they would discuss the potential need for an architect with Oscar to optimize the design and structure of the application ([00:27:44](#00:27:44)).

* **Architectural Advice and Future Collaboration**: Regarding technical guidance, Scott Bolnick, Jane Hill, and Richard Crossley agreed that while they might consult architects for advice on data structure and API access, they should not grant external parties direct access to the application itself to protect sensitive information ([00:28:47](#00:28:47)). The team concluded the meeting by agreeing to regroup in two weeks to review progress, with Richard Crossley noting they may pull the meeting forward if sufficient milestones are met ([00:29:35](#00:29:35)).
